# Output Instruction
Respond with a SINGLE JSON object and nothing else — no prose before or after it, no markdown fence required (but allowed). The object MUST match this shape exactly:
{
  "decision": "approve" | "reject" | "escalate",
  "confidence": <number 0-1>,
  "reasons": [
    { "dimension": "<e.g. completeness, consistency, contract>", "finding": "<what you found>",
      "evidence_ref": "<optional pointer>" }
  ],
  "blocking_questions": ["<string>", ...]
}
RULES:
- decision "escalate" REQUIRES at least one entry in blocking_questions.
- Every OTHER decision REQUIRES blocking_questions to be an EMPTY array.
- Prefer "escalate" over guessing when evidence is genuinely ambiguous or missing —
  a wrong confident answer is worse than an honest escalation.
- If ANY pre-check above has outcome "fail", you should almost always decision="reject"
  or "escalate", not "approve".
- reasons MUST have at least one entry.
- DESIGN NECESSITY (dimension "design_necessity", applies to every document type): decide whether the document contains anything that exists only because the design is not yet its end state. Work in this order. FIRST list every candidate item in the document: each check, guard, scanner, ledger, allowlist, fallback, phase, skip/compat/legacy state and seam. Then classify each candidate with a one-line reason as exactly one of the classes below. Only then decide.
  NOT findings (an end-state design needs these): (i) product semantics a user relies on; (ii) an interface or port contract; (iii) validation of outside input at the boundary; (iv) what an acceptance test needs to be safe and meaningful when the design is violated.
  FINDINGS (each exists only because the design is incomplete): (a) a check, scanner, ledger or allowlist whose only purpose is catching a violation of the document's OWN invariant that the design already rules out; (b) a stopgap or temporary seam; (c) a silent fallback for a missing required input; (d) a transitional or phased state: a skip/compat/legacy mode, a ratchet, or an intermediate phase.
  An item the document justifies under (i)-(iv) is not raised unless that justification is false. If any item is classified (a)-(d), you MUST return decision "reject" with a reasons entry whose dimension is "design_necessity" that names each such item, its class, and the end-state alternative. A reasons entry with dimension "design_necessity" exists ONLY to report findings: if no item is classified (a)-(d), the reasons array MUST contain NO entry with dimension "design_necessity" (do not add one to say that nothing was found, and do not use one to restate the classification of the non-findings).
